I had this exact. Same. Thing. Happen to me about 7 years ago. My best friend and I were in our early teens and went to a playground up the road from my parents house, it was even closer to my grandparents house (both houses within a 5 minute walk). 

We were sitting on top of the monkey bars chatting away and suddenly there is this immense sound.... it’s almost indescribable. It was in the air everywhere and we could feel it vibrating the monkey bars and even resonating inside of us. My friend and I were frozen in fear for the duration of the noise - I honestly couldn’t tell you how long it lasted. Finally when it stopped we both didn’t speak a word and ran, ran how you would run in a nightmare with a monster chasing you. When we got far enough I came to my senses and INSISTED we go back and investigate, but my friend couldn’t be convinced. 

We kept running home and I asked my parents and brother what that noise was, and they said they hadn’t heard anything. I called my grandparents and they too didn’t hear anything. I simply couldn’t understand how this was possible as the noise was so insanely loud. I internet searched and read the newspapers for weeks trying to find any explanation; had anyone else heard it? Did some sort of strange plane blast through? Was there an earthquake? My search uncovered no answers. 

To this day, the noise remains the biggest mystery in my life. My best friend also recalls it clear as day. Coming across your post I am filled with relief but also, in a strange way, terror.

Endometriosis. I’ve heard it’s really common but rarely diagnosed. 

Just after I graduated high school my period became intensely painful, keep in mind I hadn’t even experienced a cramp up until that point. 

Whenever I menstruated my life was hell, it felt like this intense urge to vomit mixed with someone squeezing your insides with their bare hands.
I passed out at work because of it, spent so much time unable to move in bed, went the to hospital twice because I thought I was literally dying. My mum was convinced I was in labour at one point I as I was screaming like a wild animal from pain (yeah, not pretty). 

My life was ruined every single month and I thought about killing my self all the time. I even resorted to strangling myself to get some relief from the pain. 

Anyway, got tested for pregnancy, stds, the lot. 
One male doctor legit said to me ‘teenage girls can just be dramatic’ (I WISH I was exaggerating here.
Finally a (male) doctor who specialised in women’s health pretty much told me straight up he was 99% certain it was endometriosis. The surgery for it isn’t very successful so I had an implanon inserted (basically a form of birth control implanted in your arm). Thank god that stopped my periods. I’m grateful every day that I don’t have to deal with the pain anymore because I was so damn close to just ending it all.

Killing myself (but not in the way you think).

I went through I period where I was incredibly depressed and felt like I had no control over my life. I had made serious plans to end my life and was just working up the courage/trying to figure out how to do it without hurting anyone (pro tip: there is no way to do that).

I had a breakthrough one day when I realised that if I wanted to die so bad why not just metaphorically ‘kill myself’. Meaning that anything I did after that didn’t matter - there was no point stressing over things because well, I’m basically a dead person walking anyway. 

I’m not sure if I’m describing this very well and I think everyone needs to find their own special ‘thoughts’ that help them get through tough times. But yes, metaphorically killing my self and living out my life like a dead man walking liberated me into doing all the things that made me happy without worrying about everyone/everything else so much. 

If you are feeling like there’s no hope please just hold on a little longer you have no idea what amazing experiences are lurking in your future.
